messages.subject: if then syntax
parts:
Hi all;
I apologize, but I have a mental block around if/then statements. Perhaps you can help me out of this simple stumble.

I want to obtain the residuals from a binomial model. The data in my "Presence" column are 0's and 1's (for presence/absence). The data in my "Predicted" column are probabilities from the model.

To extract the residuals:
 if 0, add Predicted
if 1, subtract Predicted

That's it! I could do it in Excel, but I have decided to break through to the other side...
thanks,
John

messages.author: b35e99045f6c74c2
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: if then syntax
parts:
Hi John,

This sounds like you need ifelse(), a vectorized if else statement.

Some sample data:

> x <- rbinom(10, 1, 0.4)
> x
 [1] 1 0 1 1 1 0 0 0 1 0
> y <- runif(10)
> y
 [1] 0.3800851 0.8145238 0.9528767 0.7491175 0.8735943 0.7262976 0.1235017
 [8] 0.7678490 0.1400231 0.2878240

> ifelse(x, y+1, y-1)
 [1]  1.3800851 -0.1854762  1.9528767  1.7491175  1.8735943 -0.2737024
 [7] -0.8764983 -0.2321510  1.1400231 -0.7121760

Here I juse is ifelse(x, ...) because x == 1 isn't necessary with 0 and 1s because these are coerced to TRUE and FALSE.

The second arguments are the vectors (of same length!) for when the first argument is TRUE and FALSE, respectively.

HTH,
Vince

messages.author: 200483e18864bf49
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: if then syntax
parts:
Vince, thanks!

For the record, 0 is coerced to FALSE and 1 to TRUE; since I wanted to add y's to 0's and subtract from 1's, I used this snippet:

ifelse(x, 1-y, y)

You got me past my block!
cheers,
John
